target_customer: Mid-size and large employers (HR, people and CSR teams) that pay per employee for workplace giving and volunteering programs
problem: Companies want employees to donate and volunteer, but legacy giving tools are clunky and employees do not use them. Deed aims for a consumer-app quality experience to lift participation.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription sold to employers
product_category: Workplace giving and employee volunteering software

founders.name: Deevee Kashi
prior_employers: Hospitality brand he helped lead (about $14M annual revenue, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: About ten years in hospitality; found volunteering hard to do, which led to the idea.

founders.name: Aske Ertmann
founders.background_notes: 15+ years building enterprise applications; former release manager of Neos CMS.

founders.name: Steve Liu
previous_startups: Boutique investment bank (founded after the financial crisis)

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly web and mobile software with integrations such as Slack and payment processing to charities, standard engineering for a small team in 2021.

defensibility.rationale: Incumbents offered similar functions, so the edge was user experience and a volunteering opportunity library, with some switching cost once embedded in HR workflows.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were not reported to copy it; Deed was instead acquired by Bonterra in March 2026.

market_need_then: Employee retention and ESG pressure in 2021 made corporate giving and volunteering budgets more visible; YC page cites 4X logo growth after public launch with names like DoorDash, Box and Lob.

branding.domain_note: Operated at joindeed.com rather than deed.com, suggesting a prefix domain; no source on how it was obtained.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positions itself as giving employees a consumer-app style experience.

rebrands.why: Naming after the Bonterra acquisition, per competitor comparison pages

brand_strength.rationale: A search found no press on the brand itself; a common English word with legal connotations that is hard to search for.

pivots.from: Consumer volunteering app (beta launched with Adidas, 2018)
pivots.to: Employer-paid workplace giving and volunteering platform
pivots.why: Not stated in sources; inferred only from the company's described history

outcome_analysis: Deed started as a consumer volunteering app in 2016 and moved to selling to employers, reaching YC in Summer 2021 with logos like Airbnb and Stripe. It raised a seed in late 2020 and a 10 million dollar Series A led by Earlybird in December 2021, then was bought by Bonterra in March 2026 to add workplace giving to its suite. Terms were not disclosed, so it is unclear whether this was a strong or soft exit.
